questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield to vehicles coming from your right. Always be ready to yield. Slow down, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: How should you park your vehicle downhill on a two-way street?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight.
Put your car in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the road edge. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane meant for oncoming traffic. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The larger vehicle.
The vehicle on the left.
The vehicle on the left must yield to the one on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the one on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the one on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver may go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is false?

options.text: Seat belts help you stay in control of your vehicle.
Only people under 18 must wear a seat belt.
Never place a child car seat in front of an airbag.
Wearing a seat belt reduces your risk of injury in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only people under 18 must wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: The law requires all passengers to wear a seat belt or use an approved child safety seat. This applies to people of all ages.

questions.question: What happens if you pass a stopped school bus with its red lights on?

options.text: You pay a large fine.
You get two points on your license.
You get a written warning.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You pay a large fine.
questions.explanation: In Vermont, passing a stopped school bus with red lights on results in a large fine and five points on your driving record. Always stop for a school bus using its warning lights and stop arm.

questions.question: Which is not a factor in how far your vehicle takes to stop?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This helps you see your blind spot. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: When getting ready to turn right, where should your vehicle be positioned?

options.text: About one foot from the right edge of the road.
About three feet from the right edge of the road.
About five feet from the right edge of the road.
As close as possible to the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: About three feet from the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Position your vehicle about three feet from the right edge of the road when preparing to turn right.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When there is a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, the driver on the side of the broken line may pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck while you are driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When the accelerator sticks, the engine will keep running even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully—only turn it far enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the radio to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is risky because drivers cannot see clearly behind their vehicles. Always walk to the back of your vehicle first to check for children and small objects before backing up.

questions.question: A green arrow turns into a solid green light. What should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
You must go straight and cannot turn.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to follow the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: A driver approaching a green traffic light:

options.text: Must yield to oncoming traffic before turning left.
Always has the right-of-way.
Must always drive straight.
Must stop before going straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to oncoming traffic before turning left.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a green light, you must let oncoming traffic pass first. You may turn when it is safe.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should stop completely, yield to crossing traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is clear?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: In bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination quickly.
Stay closer to the car ahead.
Stay farther from the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: In wet weather, increase the distance between your car and the one ahead. This gives you more time to stop safely.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk marked, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Just slow down to check if traffic is clear.
Stop far enough into the intersection so you can see 200 feet in both directions.
Stop where you can see traffic clearly before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see traffic clearly before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest point to the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.
